comparison_to_prior_leaf.documented_no_effect_terminal: Does not require a result/effect identifier when provider-authoritative semantics prove no irreversible effect exists for exact O5,D5,I5; it still requires exact identity binding, terminal immutability/no-later-execution semantics, current F5 CAS, and readback.

weak_rule_falsified.rule: Any safe terminal closure under F5 requires an immutable provider result/effect identifier.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: In the tested negative branch, provider-authoritative terminal semantics prove that execution never occurred and no irreversible effect exists. Requiring an effect identifier for an absent effect adds no safety evidence. Exact operation binding, documented no-effect terminality, no-later-execution semantics, and current F5 CAS/readback are sufficient for this negative closure within the fixture.

observations: Effectful-success closure and negative/no-effect closure have different evidence minima: the former must identify the irreversible result/effect, while the latter may instead prove that no such effect exists.

A generic terminal status remains insufficient; the positive result depends on documented provider semantics that guarantee cancellation-before-execution and forbid later execution for the exact operation identity.
Current-fence CAS/readback remains required even when provider-side evidence proves no effect, because repository finalization authority is separate from provider outcome evidence.
inference: For this exact self-local fixture, an immutable result/effect identifier is not universally necessary for safe terminal recovery. It is necessary for effect-sensitive success finalization, but a provider-authoritative terminal class with documented no-effect and no-later-execution semantics can support negative closure for exact O5,D5,I5 under current F5 CAS/readback. This does not establish any concrete provider route and does not generalize to ambiguous cancellation labels.
